definition: A Latin term meaning 'from the beginning.' Often used in contracts that are invalid from the start.
A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation, for use as evidence in court.
An impartial adviser to a court of law in a particular case (Friend of the court).
The temporary release of an accused person awaiting trial, sometimes on condition that a sum of money is lodged to guarantee their appearance.
An offense in which a police officer has the authority to make an arrest without a warrant.
An official order issued by a legal authority; the final order of a court in a suit.
A proceeding where only one party is present or represented.
A writ requiring a person under arrest to be brought before a judge or into court, especially to secure their release unless lawful grounds are shown for their detention.
A judicial order that restrains a person from beginning or continuing an action invading the legal right of another.
The right or capacity to bring an action or to appear in a court.
The intention or knowledge of wrongdoing that constitutes part of a crime (Guilty mind).
Public Interest Litigation – legal action initiated in a court of law for the protection of public interest.
A case currently under judicial consideration and therefore prohibited from public discussion.
A document by which a party authorizes an advocate to represent them in court.
A formal written order issued by a court with administrative or judicial jurisdiction.
